title: What Stands in the Way
desc: Delivery, inspection, agriculture, emergency response, AI on board — the applications are known; each one is gated by the four problems this course was about

items: Integration into existing air traffic — U-space exists on paper (Module 6); the interfaces, data and tests you built are what make it real
Trust in autonomous components — a learned model does not come with a DAL; Module 3's principles apply, the evidence is harder to produce
Security and misuse — the airport disruptions from Module 1 are not accidents; detection and identification are unsolved at scale
Regulation that keeps pace — EU 2019/947 and 2021/664 are the frame; the standards behind them (DO-178C, AIXM, ASTERIX, OLDI) are what engineers actually build against
Why drone traffic needs modeling: incidents, regulation, density (Module 1) — and why untested code never gets props (Module 2)
How aviation software is built differently: DO-178C, the 4+1 principles, confidence proportionate to risk (Module 3)
The system picture: UTM and U-space as a federation of services (Module 6)
The engineering toolbox: OpenAPI, WebFlux, message queues, CQRS, Karate (Modules 7–11)
The data aviation speaks and the laboratory to prove things in: NOTAM, METAR, AIXM, ASTERIX, OLDI, BlueSky, GIS (Modules 12–14)
Ship your practical project — working code beats slides
Fly it — and be able to explain why your code was safe to arm
Open questions? Ask now, or bring them to the next session
